description: For a receipt whose delegation certificate is signed by a contract KS256 root (a Safe, say): ask the contract whether it accepts that certificate, and return the answer as an attestation @forestrie/mcp-verify can consume offline. Reads the chain at your rpcUrl (this tool does; mcp-verify never does): eth_chainId, eth_getBlockByNumber for your block (default latest), then eth_getCode at the root and one eth_call isValidSignature(digest, signature), where digest and signature come from the receipt's certificate. Both state reads are pinned by the block's hash (EIP-1898, requireCanonical), so the hash in the attestation is the state that was read. Give the receipt, and the root as root (0x 20-byte address) or as a genesis you hold (genesis; it supplies the root when root is absent, which must then be a KS256 bootstrap root, and always supplies the chain the RPC must be on; a chain id mismatch is a problem before any further call). Returns the attestation as canonical CBOR, base64-encoded, with its fields (chain id, root address, digest, signature hash, block number, block hash, magic). Pass it to verify_receipt in mcp-verify as ks256Attestation: it then attests the certificate valid under the contract's signers at block N, which is narrower than an EOA root's offline ecrecover check; anyone with RPC can re-run the call at that block to confirm or disprove it. Refuses, with a structured problem and never an attestation, when there is no contract code at the root (an EOA root verifies by ecrecover and needs none), when the call reverts, or when the return is anything but exactly one 32-byte word, 0x1626ba7e followed by 28 zero bytes (a short return, dirty padding, extra words or an echo of the call's own data are all refused); a malformed chain id, block or hash from the RPC is an rpc_error problem. With root given beside a genesis, root is the contract asked and the genesis supplies only the expected chain (provenance.binding is explicit, chainFrom held-genesis); binding is held-genesis only when the root came from the genesis. Provenance: chain-read. Supports: none of the four questions on its own; the attestation is evidence only once mcp-verify consumes it under a root you hold.

block.description: the block to ask at; default the latest block, whose number every call is then pinned to

anyOf.description: filesystem path, read by the stdio adapter

genesis.description: a genesis document you hold: its chain id is the chain the RPC must be on, and its KS256 bootstrap root is the contract asked when root is absent — {b64: <standard base64>} (base64 is accepted as an alias), or {path: <a file the local server reads>}

anyOf.description: filesystem path, read by the stdio adapter

receipt.description: the receipt bytes; its delegation certificate supplies the digest and signature the contract is asked about — {b64: <standard base64>} (base64 is accepted as an alias), or {path: <a file the local server reads>}

root.description: the contract root's 0x-prefixed or bare 40-hex address; give this or genesis (with both, root is the contract asked and genesis supplies only the expected chain)

rpcUrl.description: your own chain RPC access; falls back to FORESTRIE_RPC_URL when omitted — the package ships no provider

name: fetch_ks256_attestation
title: Fetch KS256 attestation from chain
